sub_answers.text: Results of each of the 12 shows were determined by a 50/50 combination of votes from a jury panel and public televoting.[d40165141s3p0] The jury votes in all shows consisted of a combination of a Lithuanian jury panel and an international jury panel.[d40165141s3p0] From the second show to the semi-final the Lithuanian panel members came to a consensus to assign one set of points, while the international panel members each assigned points in descending order for their favourites and least favourites.[d40165141s3p0] The public televote ranking was converted to points from 1-8, 10 and 12 based on the number of competing artists in the respective show.[d40165141s3p0]

sub_answers.sub_question: What tie-breaking procedures and qualification criteria were specified for advancing between heats, semifinals, and the final?
sub_answers.text: Ties in the elimination shows and the semi-final were decided in favour of the entry that received the most votes from the public.[d40165141s3p0] In the final, a tie would be decided in favour of the entry that was awarded the most points by the jury.[d40165141s3p0] The competition eliminated artists across shows (five eliminated in second and third shows, one eliminated each show from fourth to tenth, leaving three artists for the final) and reduced 16 songs down to three by the tenth show, with the semi-final selecting the single winning song from those three and the final selecting the winning artist-song combination from the remaining three artists.[d40165141s3p0]

sub_answers.text: The national selection was titled "Eurovizijos" dainų konkurso nacionalinė atranka. [d40165141s1p0] The competition format was a multi-week televised series of 12 shows that paired artists independently from songs and decided results by a 50/50 combination of jury and public televote. [d40165141s3p0] The shows ran over a 12-week period with the final broadcast live on 1 March 2014 while preceding shows were pre-recorded and aired weekly. [d40165141s3p0] [d40165141s9p0]

sub_answers.text: The selection consisted of 12 shows in total, starting with a jubilee concert and continuing with elimination shows. [d40165141s3p0] The second and third shows each featured ten artists and eliminated five artists from those shows. [d40165141s3p0] From the fourth to the tenth shows one artist was eliminated in each show, leaving three artists to advance after the tenth show. [d40165141s3p0] Sixteen potential Eurovision songs competed weekly with 13 songs eliminated by the tenth show, leaving three songs; the eleventh show (the semi-final) selected the single winning song and the twelfth show (the final) featured the three remaining artists. Detail how voting influence was allocated through each stage of the competition: list the exact weightings or point conversion for domestic juries, international juries (if any), expert panels, and public televote/SMS/online across heats, semi-finals and the final, and describe whether weighting changed between rounds.
sub_answers.text: All 12 shows used a 50/50 combination of jury panel votes and public televoting/SMS to determine results in each show [d40165141s3p0]. The jury votes in all shows consisted of a Lithuanian jury panel and an international jury panel [d40165141s3p0]. From the second show to the semi-final the Lithuanian panel was required to come to a consensus to assign one set of points which were added to the international panel results [d40165141s3p0]. During each show each member of the international panel assigned points in a descending order with the highest score for their favourite and the lowest for their least favourite [d40165141s3p0]. The Lithuanian panel assigned scores from 1 to 10 to each artist from the second to the fifth shows and assigned points based on ranking starting from the sixth show [d40165141s3p0]. In the final the Lithuanian and international panels voted together, with each member awarding one set of points based on ranking [d40165141s3p0]. Public votes were cast via telephone and SMS and the ranking developed by both jury and public streams was converted to points 1–8, 10 and 12 and assigned based on the number of competing artists in the respective show [d40165141s3p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Explain the selection’s formal qualification and tie-breaking rules: specify how acts advanced from heats to semifinals and to the final (e.g., top X by televote, jury pick, combined score), the official procedure when two or more entries tied on points in any round (which voting body takes precedence, use of highest jury rank, oldest submission, or re-vote), and any provisions for wildcards, replacements or disqualifications.
sub_answers.text: The competition was staged over 12 shows with artists competing independently from songs and composers agreeing that songs could be offered to artists other than the original intended performer [d40165141s3p0]. The first show was a non-elimination jubilee concert; the second and third shows each featured ten artists with five eliminated from each show [d40165141s3p0]. From the fourth to the tenth shows one artist was eliminated in each show and the remaining three artists advanced in the competition after those shows [d40165141s3p0]. Starting from the fifth show the 16 potential Eurovision songs competed weekly and 13 songs were eliminated by the end of the tenth show leaving three songs remaining [d40165141s3p0]. The eleventh show (semi-final) selected only the winning song from the remaining three songs [d40165141s3p0]. The twelfth show (final) selected the winning artist–song combination from the remaining three artists [d40165141s3p0]. Ties in elimination shows and in the semi-final were decided in favour of the entry that received the most public votes, while ties in the final were decided in favour of the entry awarded the most points by the jury [d40165141s3p0].
